frequency_question: How often do statutory congressional review periods result in successfully enacted joint resolutions of disapproval against major executive foreign agreements?
membership_rule: Includes all formal major bilateral or multilateral pacts submitted under statutory review mechanisms (such as the AECA or similar frameworks) where Congress has a defined window to pass a joint resolution of disapproval, evaluated since 1976. Excludes non-binding memoranda and routine commercial export licenses.

cases.name: 2016 JCPOA related nuclear framework review (hypothetical statutory equivalent window)
2019 Yemen-related emergency arms sales congressional disapproval resolutions

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named major historical test cases identified; believed to be the complete population of major contested strategic/nuclear/arms review cycles matching the structural constraint.
known_gaps: Historical minor notifications under the Arms Export Control Act that never reached floor votes are excluded as non-events, though the denominator of all formal notifications is much larger.
validity_reason: The constitutional and statutory balance of power regarding executive agreements and legislative vetoes has remained stable for decades.
